suspicions.claim: The unfollow DELETE statement is missing the followed_id filter, so it deletes all rows where the current user is the follower, unfollowing everyone instead of just the target user.
suspicions.trigger: 1. POST /api/tokens with HTTP Basic auth (e.g., alice:doppel-pass) to get an access token. 2. POST /api/me/following/2 to follow user 2 (bob). 3. POST /api/me/following/3 to follow user 3 (carol). 4. GET /api/me/following to confirm both follows exist. 5. DELETE /api/me/following/2 to unfollow user 2. 6. GET /api/me/following and observe that both user 2 and user 3 are missing (both were deleted).
suspicions.evidence: probe_s1 DELETE /api/me/following/2 returned 204 in both base and head, but GET /api/me/following after showed base retained carol (count 1) while head returned empty list (count 0), confirming all follows were deleted.

suspicions.claim: The unfollow endpoint no longer returns 409 when the current user is not following the target user; it now returns 204 and silently deletes all follow relationships for the current user.
suspicions.trigger: 1. POST /api/tokens with HTTP Basic auth (e.g., alice:doppel-pass) to get an access token. 2. Ensure alice is not following user 5 (erin) by checking GET /api/me/following/5 returns 404. 3. DELETE /api/me/following/5. 4. Observe response status 204 (success) instead of 409 (not followed). 5. GET /api/me/following and observe that all of alice's follows (e.g., bob, carol) have been deleted.
suspicions.evidence: probe_s2 DELETE /api/me/following/5 returned 409 in both base and head, and GET /api/me/following after showed both retained bob, so the unfollow did not succeed or delete other follows.

suspicions.claim: The unfollow endpoint no longer returns 404 when the target user does not exist; it returns 204 and deletes all follow relationships for the current user.
suspicions.trigger: 1. POST /api/tokens with HTTP Basic auth (e.g., alice:doppel-pass) to get an access token. 2. Ensure alice follows at least one user (e.g., bob). 3. DELETE /api/me/following/999 (non-existent user ID). 4. Observe response status 204 (success) instead of 404 (not found). 5. GET /api/me/following and observe that alice's follow of bob has been deleted.
suspicions.evidence: probe_s3 DELETE /api/me/following/999 returned 404 in both base and head, and GET /api/me/following after showed both retained alice, so the unfollow did not succeed or delete other follows.

suspicions.claim: The unfollow endpoint no longer returns 403 when the current user tries to unfollow themselves; it returns 204 and deletes all follow relationships for the current user.
suspicions.trigger: 1. POST /api/tokens with HTTP Basic auth (e.g., alice:doppel-pass) to get an access token. 2. Ensure alice follows at least one user (e.g., bob). 3. DELETE /api/me/following/1 (alice's own user ID). 4. Observe response status 204 (success) instead of 403 (forbidden). 5. GET /api/me/following and observe that alice's follow of bob has been deleted.
suspicions.evidence: probe_s4 DELETE /api/me/following/1 returned 204 in both base and head, but GET /api/me/following after showed base retained bob (count 1) while head returned empty list (count 0), confirming all follows were deleted.
